title: The Quack Frog
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: Once upon a time a Frog came forth from his home in the marshes and proclaimed to all the world that he was a learned physician, skilled in drugs and able to cure all diseases. Among the crowd was a Fox, who called out, "You a doctor! Why, how can you set up to heal others when you cannot even cure your own lame legs and blotched and wrinkled skin?"

questions.prompt: According to the passage, where does the Frog come from?
options: A distant kingdom across the sea
A cave in the mountains
His home in the marshes
A village of other frogs

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Frog claim to be?
options: A learned physician, skilled in drugs and able to cure all diseases
A wise judge who settles disputes fairly
A famous singer known throughout the marshes
A skilled builder of bridges and dams

questions.prompt: According to the passage, who challenges the Frog's claim?
options: Another Frog
A passing traveller
A group of villagers
A Fox

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Fox say the Frog cannot cure in himself?
options: His fear of larger animals
His own lame legs and blotched, wrinkled skin
His inability to leave the marshes
His weak and croaking voice

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what point is the Fox making by mentioning the Frog's own condition?
options: The Frog is too old to be a real physician
The Frog's remedies are simply too expensive for most people
A claim to heal others rings hollow if you cannot even help yourself
The Frog should treat foxes before treating frogs

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why might the crowd have been inclined to believe the Frog before the Fox spoke up?
options: The Frog proclaimed his skill boldly and publicly, with no one yet questioning it
The crowd had already seen the Frog cure someone
The Fox was known to be an unreliable source of doubt
The Frog offered his services for free

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "proclaimed" mean in "proclaimed to all the world"?
options: Whispered secretly to a few
Denied quietly to himself
Wrote down in a private letter
Announced publicly and boldly

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "blotched" describe about the Frog's skin?
options: Smooth and evenly colored
Marked with discolored patches
Covered in soft fur
Shiny and freshly washed

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does it mean that the Frog wanted to "set up" as a healer?
options: To pack up his belongings and leave
To repair something that was broken
To establish himself in that role publicly
To arrange a meeting with the crowd

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable, given its closing line?
options: Someone claiming to fix others' problems should first be able to fix their own
Frogs make poor doctors compared to other animals
Foxes are always more honest than frogs
Marshes are unsuitable places to practice medicine

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Frog claim he is able to do?
options: Predict the weather
Speak every language
Live forever without aging
Cure all diseases

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how does the Fox address the Frog directly?
options: "You a fraud!"
"You a doctor!"
"You a fool!"
"You a liar!"

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what two physical problems does the Fox point out?
options: A weak voice and poor eyesight
A missing leg and a broken tail
Lame legs and blotched, wrinkled skin
Slow movement and constant hunger

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why is the Fox's challenge especially damaging to the Frog's claim?
options: It uses visible evidence anyone in the crowd could also observe
It comes from an animal known for practicing medicine himself
It is delivered privately, so the Frog cannot respond publicly
It focuses on something unrelated to the Frog's medical claim

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the story suggest about judging someone's claimed expertise?
options: Trust anyone who speaks confidently in front of a crowd
Assume all public claims of skill are automatically false
Rely only on how long someone has practiced their claimed skill
Look at whether their own condition matches what they claim to be able to fix

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "learned" mean in "he was a learned physician"?
options: Elderly and experienced
Educated and knowledgeable
Wealthy and well-connected
Feared and respected

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A Frog successfully cures a sick Fox in front of a crowd
A Fox asks the Frog to teach him medicine
A Frog claims to cure all diseases, but a Fox points out he cannot even heal himself
A crowd chases the Frog away before he can speak
